The Pros and Cons of Flat Commercial Roofing

One really popular look for commercial roofing is the flat roof. This common roofing type can be seen in various buildings in cities around the world. In this article, we will discuss what the pros and cons are to using a flat commercial roof.

One of the biggest advantages that flat commercial roofing has is the price point. Flat roofs are extremely cost-effective. They use quite a bit less square footage for materials than a sloped roof. Fewer materials will naturally drive the cost down.

And if you want to save even more money, flat commercial roofing can do that when it is installed. Flat roofs do not take as much time to install, so therefore, your cost will be driven down even more. And, since they are easy to install, a person is generally billed less from their building contractor.

What is great about flat roofs is that there are many different kinds of roofing materials that can be used. Built up roofing may strike some fancy, while others prefer rubber rolled roofing. There is also bitumen, modified bitumen, PVC, TPO, and EPDM. What's more, is that these roofs come in colors! While many prefer to stick with white, it is nice to know that other colors can use used as well. Many will stick with white as it further helps to save money by reducing the energy costs due to the reflective nature of the material.

Have you ever thought about having your air conditioner on the roof? Most people do not think of this. But when you have flat commercial roofing, one popular option is to do just that. And you do not need to just stop at the air conditioner. Solar panel and satellite dishes are also installed on flat roofs. And since there is no slope, they are easier to install there as well. Plus, as an extra added benefit, these items are harder to see from far away on a flat roof than a slanted roof.

Now let's think about when people have to get up on your roof. If you have flat commercial roofing, it is safer for people to be walking around up there. Not that you will have people up there every day, but if there is maintenance that needs to be done or a repair that needs to be made, you will not have to worry about it as much.

So now that we have talked about all the advantages of flat commercial roofing, we need to switch gears to the disadvantages. The biggest disadvantage is that this type of roof has very poor drainage. And due to this, there is often standing water. We all know that standing water can lead to a lot of damage to not only the outside of the building but the inside as well.

If you are looking into having flat commercial roofing installed for your business, it is in your best interest to contact a company that is experienced. Look for one that is affordable and has a trusted reputation to do the best high-quality work!
